_comment: Generate, review, animate, and package a configurable four-direction character for RPG Maker XP, VX, VX Ace, MV, or MZ. MZ is the default.
_comment_prompt: Create an RPG Maker character spritesheet; default to MZ and an adult male human chibi base character with non-explicit doll-like anatomy and no clothing or equipment.

TASK.instruction: Follow this JSON array in order; no external instructions are required. Resolve every `{{...}}` placeholder before a call and use its default silently when the user supplied no value. Resolve RPG Maker version case-insensitively, strip an optional `RPG Maker` prefix, normalize VXAce to VX Ace, and accept only XP, VX, VX Ace, MV, or MZ. A `map` modifier means: resolve the named variable first (using `default` as that variable's default), replace the whole placeholder with the mapped JSON value, and stop if no key matches. Thus the map on create_character.size is also the version enum; never ask the user for a technical size. Derive export cells separately: XP=32x48, VX/VX Ace=32x32, MV/MZ=48x48. Never put the version in the PixelLab description. Require an explicit current-user request to run this paid recipe and callable PixelLab MCP create_character, get_character, and animate_character tools. If MCP is unavailable or unconfigured, stop and show https://www.pixellab.ai/mcp; do not substitute REST. Create the declared output directory empty, or append the lowest free suffix beginning at -2; never overwrite a run. Before spending, show the resolved create_character body and planned animate_character arguments, identifying character_id as the fresh ID of the ultimately approved candidate. Disclose approximately 5 generations total (one character generation plus four directional animation jobs) and wait for explicit approval. This approval covers one animation of the ultimately approved candidate. Every regeneration needs separate approval for one additional character generation; never retry a paid call automatically.
TASK.verify: Both user-facing variables and the inline size map resolve; the version is supported; the MCP tools are callable; the output directory is new and empty; and the user approved the resolved paid chain.

MCP create_character.description: {{character | default: adult male human chibi base character, non-explicit doll-like anatomy, no clothing or equipment}}, readable four-direction top-down map sprite, clean silhouette, consistent identity and proportions, flat pixel art, limited palette, hard edges
MCP create_character.size: {{RPG Maker version | map: {"XP": 48, "VX": 32, "VX Ace": 32, "MV": 48, "MZ": 48} | default: MZ}}

TASK.instruction: Poll get_character with the fresh ID returned by create_character; never resubmit automatically. Save each completed rotation unchanged at the path below and build the contact sheet only as a review aid. Do not animate yet. A regeneration uses the next unused candidate directory (02, 03, and so on) and never overwrites a prior candidate.
TASK.verify: The saved south, west, east, and north rotations are readable transparent PNGs, retain their returned pixels, and appear correctly labeled in the contact sheet.

TASK.instruction:
Display the contact sheet and render this Markdown checkpoint exactly: `🎭 **Character ready — choose the next step**

1. **Continue animating** — create the engine-appropriate walk frames for all four directions.
2. **Regenerate character** — describe what to change; this adds another paid character generation and will be cost-gated.
3. **Stop here** — keep the four directional base sprites without creating an animated engine sheet.

Reply **1 / 2 / 3**, or describe the changes you want.` Wait. Continue uses the already-approved animation call without another approval. Regenerate collects changes, shows and waits for approval of one additional create_character call (~1 generation), changes only the description, uses a fresh ID and the next candidate directory, then repeats this checkpoint. Stop makes no animation call and reports that the saved rotations are not an engine-ready animated sheet. Any other paid-plan change requires fresh approval.
TASK.verify: Animation starts only after Continue; each regeneration is separately approved and uses a fresh ID; Stop makes no later paid call.

TASK.instruction: Only after Continue, copy the reviewed rotations unchanged to approved/rotations. Call animate_character once on that fresh character ID with mode=template, template_animation_id=walking-4-frames, animation_name=four-direction walk, directions=[south, west, east, north], and ai_freedom=0. Poll get_character until all four direction jobs complete or one fails; never retry automatically. Save each direction's four returned frames unchanged and in returned order as 01.png through 04.png.
TASK.verify: South, west, east, and north each have exactly four readable transparent frames saved unchanged in returned order.

TASK.instruction: After successful animation, package the approved pixels for {{RPG Maker version | default: MZ}} without repainting. Rows are fixed: south=1 Down, west=2 Left, east=3 Right, north=4 Up. First select only the poses the profile will deliver. XP uses all four returned walk frames in columns 1,2,3,4, matching playback 1→2→3→4, and never uses the static rotation; output rpg-maker-character.png with 32x48 cells at 4x4 (128x192). VX/VX Ace/MV/MZ use the reviewed static rotation in column 2 and a visually verified, chronologically ordered pair of distinct opposing strides from the four walk frames in columns 1 and 3, matching playback 2→1→2→3; stop if the pair is ambiguous, duplicated, or jumps against standing. Output $rpg-maker-character.png at 3x4: VX/VX Ace use 32x32 cells (96x128), and MV/MZ use 48x48 cells (144x192). Then normalize only those delivered poses: find each pose's alpha>0 bounds, reject empty poses, and remove only fully transparent margins. Within each row, align the cropped poses to one bottom-center origin and compute their union. Let maxW and maxH be the maximum row-union width and height; apply one nearest-neighbor scale min(1, CW/maxW, CH/maxH) to every delivered pose, then bottom-center each in an exact CWxCH cell using only transparent padding. PixelLab's resolved size and returned canvas dimensions are not export dimensions. Never crop alpha>0 pixels, upscale, or fit poses independently. Create a looping rpg-maker-character-engine-playback.gif using the engine order and explicit frame disposal, then verify its coalesced frames. Create a separate rpg-maker-character-inspection-grid.png labeled `Inspection aid — expected grid overlay`; the grid never alters the sheet.
TASK.verify: The sheet, looping playback GIF, and separate grid decode; the GIF has explicit disposal and coalesces faithfully. XP is 128x192 with 32x48 cells, no `$`, and clean 1→2→3→4→1 playback. VX/VX Ace is 96x128 with 32x32 cells; MV/MZ is 144x192 with 48x48 cells; VX through MZ use `$`, Down/Left/Right/Up rows, and movement/standing/movement columns. Only delivered poses affect scaling; every alpha>0 pixel stays in its cell; transparency is preserved; and previews show no scale, center, baseline, seam, or standing-pose jitter.
